note: Vectors for the registration RECORD (docs/contracts/panel-tab-registration-v1.schema.json). The SEMANTIC refusals — an id the inventory does not declare (`unknown-tab-id`), two tabs claiming one `order` (`order-collision` / `duplicate-order`), a registration that renumbers itself (`order-mismatch`), an order outside the reserved band (`order-out-of-range`), the same id twice (`duplicate-id`) — are the registry's, not the schema's: they need the inventory to judge, and they are proven in xr-core/ui/panel/tests/tab-registry.test.mjs. This file proves the STRUCTURAL half, which is what a schema can honestly own.

accept.case: the site tab, exactly as ui/panel/tabs.json declares it
a tab that does not require an identity scope (update is per-installation, not per-identity)

refuse.why: A registration may not carry copy. A tab title is a msgid; a string here is untranslatable prose that no l10n lane would ever see.
Without a msgid the frame has nothing to render as a title, and the tab strip would fall back to the id — a machine token shown to a user.
A string order is how two tabs end up '10' and 10 sorting differently in the strip.
Fractional orders let a subsystem take 10.5 and quietly sit between two declared tabs that nobody asked it to move.
The field decides whether the tab is offered per-identity. A truthy string ('yes', 'identity') decides it by accident, in a renderer, at the worst moment.
The id is the key the inventory, the allowlist and the deep link all share; a number here matches nothing and refuses nothing.
